title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is part of Grothendieck's case analysis of certain algebraic group schemes M_{ρ,σ} attached to a pair (ρ,σ) of elements of G = GL_2 in 'variations sur l'équation des lacets'. T_ρ and T_σ are the tori (commutative group schemes) of elements commuting with ρ and σ. T_0 is a fixed torus, apparently the diagonal one. SG = SL_2.

M°_{ρ,σ} consists of symbols (u,a,b)·f with u∈T_0, a∈T_ρ, b∈T_σ, f∈G, subject to determinant conditions. It has a homomorphism Θ: M° → G. Its quotient by the subgroup 𝔖^+_{ρ,σ} ≅ SL_2 is the commutative group 𝒯°_{ρ,σ} ≅ T_ρ ×_{G_m} T_σ, the fibre product over the determinant.

Step (5°), from the previous page: R°_{ρ,σ} = Θ^{-1}(G_m), where G_m is the centre (scalars) of G. This gives an extension 1 → SR° → R° → G_m → 1.

This page:
- (71) gives an explicit parametrisation of R° by triples (μ,a,b) with det a = det b = μ². The element is (j_{T_0}(μ²), a, b)·j_G(μ^{-2}).
- (72) defines the cocharacter j(μ) = diag(μ,1), i.e. G_m → T_0 ⊂ G.
- (73)–(74): the composite R° ↪ M° → 𝒯° ≅ T_ρ ×_{G_m} T_σ is a Galois covering. More precisely there is a cartesian square of commutative group schemes: R° = (T_ρ ×_{G_m} T_σ) ×_{G_m, μ↦μ²} G_m. So R° is the pullback of the determinant along the squaring map. It is a μ_2-torsor, which is étale when 2 is invertible.
- (75) Proposition: R° = Centre(M°).
- Proof, finished on the next page:
  - The centre maps into the centre G_m of the quotient M°/SR° ≅ G, hence lies in R°.
  - Conversely, M° is generated by R° and 𝔖^+ ≅ SL_2, because R° → 𝒯° is surjective.
  - R° is commutative.
  - Each element of R° acts on SL_2 by int j_G(μ²)·int j_G(μ^{-2}) = id.
  - Finally R° ∩ SL_2 = μ_2 = Ker(R° → 𝒯°).

In modern terms: M° is a central product (R° × SL_2)/μ_2, i.e. a reductive group with derived group SL_2 and connected-centre-type radical R°. This is the analogue of GL_2 = (G_m × SL_2)/μ_2.
errors: (72) as transcribed reads j(μ) = (μ 1; 0 1) ∈ ΓSG. This cannot be right on two counts. The upper triangular matrix (μ 1; 0 1) is not a homomorphism G_m → T_0. Moreover det j(μ) = μ, so j(μ) is not in SL_2. The intended map is surely j(μ) = diag(μ,1) ∈ ΓG (not SG), consistent with the NB that det j_G(μ^{-2}) = μ^{-2}.

(71) seems to omit the sign/scalar factor λ (λ² = det u) that appears on the previous page (f = λu^{-1}) and on the next page ('λ j…'). It also takes u only of the special form j_{T_0}(μ²). The '≃' must therefore be understood up to this normalisation, or the parametrisation is incomplete as written.
'revêtement galoisien' (étale crossed out) holds as an étale μ_2-cover only where 2 is invertible. In characteristic 2, μ ↦ μ² is radicial.

ideas.what: Preimage of the centre G_m of GL_2 under Θ gives a commutative group R° fitting into a cartesian square with the squaring map on G_m, i.e. a μ_2-cover of T_ρ ×_{G_m} T_σ
ideas.modern_name: pullback of determinant along Kummer isogeny; μ_2-torsor / double cover of a torus
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard (Kummer theory, structure of reductive groups)

ideas.what: Centre of M° equals R°; M° generated by R° and SL_2 with intersection μ_2
ideas.modern_name: central product decomposition (R° × SL_2)/μ_2 of a reductive group (radical × derived group)
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical structure theory of reductive groups (Chevalley, SGA3 Demazure–Grothendieck)
ideas.where_published: SGA 3 (general structure of reductive group schemes); this specific instance unpublished

deep.surprise_reason: A routine verification within a long case analysis: computing the centre of an auxiliary group scheme built from GL_2 and two tori. The central-product structure is standard. Nothing here appears to be a new result or connection beyond the (unpublished) overall program.
transcription_corrections: (72): matrix should read diag(μ,1), i.e. (μ 0; 0 1), and the membership is likely ΓG rather than ΓSG. The '1' in the upper-right is probably a misreading.
In (71) the NB reads roughly 'NB. le dét est 1 car det j_G(μ^{-2}) = μ^{-2}', and the right margin adds 'det a = det b = μ²'.
(73): the crossed-out word before 'galoisien' is likely 'étale'. The quotient is 𝒯°_{ρ,σ} = M°_{ρ,σ}/𝔖^+_{ρ,σ}.
Below (74) the arrow G_m → G_m is μ ↦ μ².
